newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices fall as monsoon at peak.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices fall as monsoon at peak.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Monday fell on sluggish mill buying and higher supplies, dealers said.
Cotton arrivals improved amid unloading by stockist after reports of the satisfactory progress of the monsoon in India.
Expectations of a higher new crop in the coming cotton season also prompted some offerings by the state-owned agencies.

In spot deals Punjab saw-ginned fell by 10 rupees at 1,800/1,840 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Bengal-deshi slumped by 50/55 rupees at 945/1,000 rupees per maund. In the Gujarat segment Kalyan cotton fell by 100 rupees at 14,000/14,300 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while wagad cotton fell by 200/300 rupees at 12,700/12,800 rupees per candy.
"Absence of fresh export quota by the Indian government also induced some of the state-owned agencies to unload unsold stock in the domestic market," one broker said.
